subject: Cortex Systems - marketplace onboarding sprint & private-offer playbook
messages:
From: Angela Morris <angela.morris@cortexsys.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cortexsys.com
Date: Mon, 11 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP request + procurement questions for private offer

Hi Aditya / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Cortex is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed for the LLM inferencing. Procurement asked me to get a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) that ties our evaluation milestones to the private-offer purchase path (AWS private offer preferred; we are also evaluating Azure).

High level asks from procurement:
- A 6‑8 week evaluation plan with acceptance criteria (tech + business).
- Confirmation of billing entity, invoice cadence, and whether Redwood can accept purchase orders mapped to an AWS private offer.
- A sample timeline for legal review + signing (DocuSign is required on our side).

Could you send a draft MAP and an outline of the billing/PO path by EOD tomorrow? Procurement wants to lock milestones into their internal sprint.

Best,
Angela Morris
Head of Corporate Procurement
Cortex Systems
[Attachment: Cortex_RFP_v1.pdf]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Angela Morris <angela.morris@cortexsys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Mar 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request + procurement questions for private offer

Angela — thanks for the clear asks. I attached a first-cut MAP and the evaluation checklist for your engineering and procurement teams. High-level response inline, and a proposed sprint with owners below.

Billing & PO:
- Redwood can accept a PO tied to an AWS Marketplace private offer. The private offer flow will generate an invoice from Redwood (via AWS billing) once the private offer is accepted and seats/commit are provisioned.
- Payment terms: standard Net30; we can discuss Net45 for enterprise procurement if needed.
- Billing entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (we will provide full remit details on the private-offer package).

Proposed evaluation MAP (6 weeks):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + environment access (Cortex infra owner + Redwood onboarding). Owner: Laura Bennett
2) Week 1–2: Performance and throughput baseline (target P95 latency, sample prompts). Owner: Cortex eng / Redwood solutions
3) Week 3: Security/compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence + access controls). Owner: Priyom Das
4) Week 4–5: Acceptance testing with production prompts; regression metrics. Owner: Cortex eng + Aditya Rao
5) Week 6: Sign-off & private-offer acceptance (procurement/legal). Action: procurement to accept AWS private offer, Redwood to issue invoice.

Attachments I shared: Cortex_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, Redwood_Eval_Checklist.xlsx, AWS_PrivateOffer_Template.pdf.

Next steps: can we get 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the MAP with procurement and engineering? I can give a short runthrough of the private-offer billing path.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
[Attachment: Cortex_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf]
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Angela Morris <angela.morris@cortexsys.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request + procurement questions for private offer

Adding a quick technical note on the billing variants and acceptance gates — cc'ing Angela so procurement sees the nuance.

- AWS private offer (recommended): Cortex accepts the private offer in AWS console; AWS will surface a contract ID; once accepted, Redwood can provision dedicated capacity and the first invoice will be generated through AWS billing. This aligns best with existing Cortex purchasing flows and provides a clean invoice link back to the private offer.
- Azure Marketplace: similar private-offer pattern exists but requires separate legal onboarding; if Cortex prefers Azure, timeline may stretch by ~1–2 weeks.
- SLA / Acceptance: recommend we include a short production-validation gate: 72-hour smoke window with agreed metrics (P95 < X ms, token-cost drift < Y%). If metrics pass, procurement triggers PO acceptance.

I'll be available for the walkthrough tomorrow with a slide on the private-offer acceptance UI.

— Priyom
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: AWS_PrivateOffer_Template.pdf]
From: Procurement <procurement@cortexsys.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Angela Morris <angela.morris@cortexsys.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request + procurement questions for private offer

Aditya / Priyom,

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — helpful. A few clarifying requests from legal/procurement before we lock dates:
- Please provide a sample invoice that shows the line items as they will appear when billed through AWS (we need to reconcile to our AP system).
- Confirm whether Redwood invoices will show an AWS chargeback reference (yes/no).
- If we accept the private offer, who signs the DocuSign — procurement or an authorized server owner? We typically need both the commercial signature and a technical acceptance sign-off.
- Can Redwood support a single PO that references the private offer contract ID and splits billing across two Cortex cost centers? (If not, we'll need to route invoices through our central finance team.)

If you can answer these by EOD Friday we can keep the 6‑week cadence and lock the final kickoff for Mon 18 Mar.

Procurement Team
Cortex Systems
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@cortexsys.com>, Angela Morris <angela.morris@cortexsys.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP request + procurement questions for private offer

Hi Procurement / Angela — answers below and next actions attached.

- Sample invoice: attached sample_invoice_aws.csv (shows line items: private-offer commitment, metered usage adjustments, taxes). Will format to Cortex AP schema on request.
- AWS chargeback reference: yes — AWS includes the private-offer contract ID on the invoice; we will also include a reference in Redwood's invoice metadata so your AP can map it back.
- DocuSign signature flow: we can set DocuSign to require two signers — an authorized commercial signee and a technical acceptance signee. We'll include the 72‑hour smoke window acceptance language in the SOW.
- Split billing / cost centers: AWS private offer invoices typically come under a single invoice; splitting across cost centers is handled by Cortex tagging (account/sub-account). If Cortex cannot tag, we can generate a supplemental internal allocation CSV for your finance team.

Next actions and timeline:
- Fri 15 Mar: I upload the DocuSign package for the AWS private offer (link below). Please identify commercial signer + tech acceptance signer.
- Mon 18 Mar: Kickoff call (30m) — onboarding + environment access. Owner: Laura Bennett.
- Weeks 1–2: Baseline perf tests. Owner: Cortex eng / Redwood (Priyom).
- Week 3: Security evidence handoff (Priyom).
- Week 6: Acceptance + private-offer acceptance in AWS console + first invoice generation.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-cortex-private-offer
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/4827

Attachments included: Cortex_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, Redwood_Eval_Checklist.xlsx, AWS_PrivateOffer_Template.pdf, sample_invoice_aws.csv

Let me know the names/emails of the two signers and we'll schedule the kickoff for Monday.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
